- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 20-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and model forecasts are rising, check for mean reversion; if price has been rising for 5+ days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.27–0.53) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 10-day SMA as anchor for mid-range forecast.
- If model forecast is >+5% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 70, model tends to overestimate; apply a 2–4% downward bias if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model often fails to adjust; force a 1–2% downward correction to avoid “sentiment-blind” overconfidence.
